history.evaluator_summary: Adds a virtual workspace (resolver 2) with onlypassword-core (lib, non-default features insecure-fast-kdf and test-hooks) and onlypassword-cli (bin 'onlypassword'). It declares no dependencies, carries forbid(unsafe_code) and the cfg_attr clippy denies in both crate roots, and has one trivial test per crate and a committed Cargo.lock. I ran cargo build (produces target/debug/onlypassword), cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings (clean, with unwrap in tests) and cargo test (2 pass). I did not re-run gate.sh; I relied on the stated pass. No crypto or secret code is involved.

Adds the Error enum (identical to architecture.md, fixed-string Display, std::error::Error, Result alias) and SecretString/SecretVec/SecretBytes<N> secret containers. Each derives Zeroize+ZeroizeOnDrop, has a manual redacted Debug, and has no Display, Serialize or Clone. Only the zeroize dependency was added (derive feature). The new Cargo.lock entries are zeroize_derive and its proc-macro dependencies. I ran cargo test and all 8 core tests pass. No blocker or major findings.

Adds rng module: fill_random, random_array::<N>, uniform(n) over an internal RandomSource trait whose only implementation is OsSource (getrandom::fill, errors mapped to Error::Rng). uniform uses from_be_bytes on 8 bytes and threshold n.wrapping_neg() % n exactly as architecture.md says; a width-generic reject_sample helper is tested with an exhaustive 8-bit source. Only getrandom was added (it is in approved-deps). I ran cargo test -p onlypassword-core: 17 passed. I read the diff and found no other randomness source, no unwrap/panic in non-test code, and no unsafe. Only minor test-quality notes remain.

Adds onlypassword_core::base32 with encode (unpadded upper case), tolerant decode, decode_strict (rejects non-zero trailing bits), parse_totp_secret (10..=128 bytes), normalize_totp_secret and a lower-case strict hex codec. Errors are InvalidInput with a fixed message, there is no panic path in non-test code, and no dependency was added. I ran the 9 base32 tests and they pass. Every acceptance criterion has a test that can fail. Findings are minor only.

Adds crypto::aead (XChaCha20-Poly1305 via the approved crate, random 24-byte nonce per seal, AD argument, open maps every failure to Error::Authentication and returns a SecretVec), crypto::hkdf (extract+expand and expand-from-PRK, fixed 32-byte output, exact INFO labels matching CS §3.5) and a cfg(test) vector-loading helper with its own hex decoder. I ran cargo test (41 passed, including xchacha_kat, chacha_rfc8439_kat, rfc5869_kat, every_bit_flip_fails, nonces_differ_between_calls, the testutil missing/empty tests). KATs load spec/vectors via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR; the deterministic-nonce path is private/cfg(test) only. Dependencies are all in approved-deps.txt. No blocker or major issues; only minor notes.

Adds crypto::kdf with KdfParams (DEFAULT/MIN/cfg-gated FAST_FOR_TESTS, validate, validate_strict), NFKC password normalization returning a zeroizing SecretVec, a separate creation-path length check counted after NFKC, and argon2id() using Argon2id v0x13 with no secret/AD, 32-byte output wrapped in SecretBytes. Params are validated before Argon2 allocates. argon2 (alloc, zeroize; no parallel) and unicode-normalization are on the approved list. I ran the kdf tests with --all-features (13 pass) and a plain build; code matches CS 3.1, 3.3 and 10. No blocker or major findings.

Adds crypto::keys with SecretKey (generate/to_text/from_text/from_key_file_text), MasterKey::derive (Argon2id then HKDF extract+expand, salt=kdf_salt, IKM=pw_key||SK, INFO_MK), VaultKey/ItemKey, and K_iw/K_fa via HKDF-Expand. It matches CS 3.2-3.5. Key types derive Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop, have redacted Debug, and are not Clone/Copy. Parsing is panic-free (uses str::get, no indexing) and every failure is InvalidInput. I ran the 11 keys/hkdf tests and all pass. The independent-recompute tests use the argon2 and hkdf crates directly with literal label strings.

Adds core::item (Item, ItemKind, TotpConfig, CustomField, ItemId, validate, to_plaintext/from_plaintext) with serde/serde_json. I ran the 13 item tests (all pass) and read the whole diff. Wire format, key order, two-pass read, deny_unknown_fields, required nullable keys, schema probe, limits, TOTP canonical rule and Debug redaction all match CS section 7 and are covered by tests that can fail. One real defect: the output buffer capacity is a heuristic (sum + sum/8 + 256) that is too small whenever strings need JSON escaping (control characters expand 6x as \u00XX, quotes/backslashes 2x). serde_json then grows the Vec by realloc, leaving a copy of the plaintext (passwords, TOTP secret) in freed, un-zeroized heap memory. CS section 7 specifies a preallocated Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> precisely to avoid that, so REQ-SEC-002 is not met for such items. No test covers it.

Adds core::item: Item/ItemKind/TotpConfig/TotpAlgorithm/CustomField/ItemId, validate(), compact fixed-order schema-1 serialization into a Zeroizing<Vec> with exact preallocation (counting-writer pass), and two-pass reading (i64 schema probe without deny_unknown_fields, then strict deny_unknown_fields structs with deserialize_with 'required' for username/password/totp, no default/flatten). serde and serde_json are in approved-deps. I ran `cargo test -p onlypassword-core item`: 14/14 pass. By reading, the tests assert exact bytes, per-key missing rows (including the three nullable keys absent), duplicates at top level/totp/fields entry, schema 0/2 with unknown fields, canonical TOTP secret cases and Debug redaction. No blocker or major issues found; two spec-deviation notes the owner should see (LimitExceeded on oversize write; to_plaintext/from_plaintext carrying timestamps) are recorded in agent-notes/spec-issues.md.

Adds crates/onlypassword-core/src/format.rs: a key-free VaultFile parse/serialize codec using a bounds-checked Reader (checked_add, slice get, try_into; no indexing or unwrap in non-test code). Parse follows CS 9 steps 1-7 in order (length incl. LimitExceeded over 512 MiB, magic, version, flags, kdf id/version, KdfParams::validate mapped to Corrupt, structure). The record_count is bounded by remaining/146 before Vec::with_capacity, so no allocation is fed an untrusted count; body_ct is copied only after record_len and body_ct_len are verified against remaining bytes. Strict ascending ids, trailing bytes and trailer position are checked. I ran `cargo test --all-features format`: 12/12 pass. The tests use a hand-built image from the spec offsets (independent of serialize), and cover versions, flags, magic, KDF bounds, multi-fault ordering, record_count/record_len extremes, truncation at every length, and oversize input. No new deps; only a pub mod line added to lib.rs. Minor gaps only.

Adds crates/onlypassword-core/src/seal.rs: wrap_vk/unwrap_vk (AD_VK = label || 82-byte header prefix), seal_item/open_record (fresh IK, nonces, AD_IK/AD_BODY per CS 6.3), compute/verify_trailer (AEAD over SHA-256 of file prefix with K_fa, CS 6.4), build_image, and open_vault. Records can only be opened through OpenedVault, which open_vault constructs only after unwrap and trailer verification, so no record is decrypted before the trailer passes. Labels, field order and widths match the spec by reading, and the independent-AD test confirms them with the chacha20poly1305 crate directly. Error ordering matches CS 9 steps 8-12: the AEAD failure comes first, then JSON schema != 1 gives UnsupportedVersion, then a record/JSON schema mismatch gives Corrupt. I ran cargo test (all 95 core tests plus the others pass, including the 9 seal tests) and cargo clippy --all-targets (clean). Only minor issues remain.

Adds storage.rs with write_atomic (temp file via create_new, 0600, sync_all, rename, dir fsync, symlink resolved first, temp removed on failure), create_new_atomic (hard_link, no rename fallback, pub(crate) hook), read_bounded (metadata check plus take(max+1)), and same_file_path (canonical, canonical parent plus name when missing). It follows CS 6.6. tempfile is on the approved list and used only as a dev-dependency. I ran the 12 storage tests as a non-root user (uid 1000) and all pass, so the unwritable-directory test really exercises the failure path. clippy is clean. No crypto or secret handling is involved. Remaining issues are minor.

Adds Clock/SystemClock and Vault::{create, create_with_key, unlock, lock, kdf_params, set_clock (cfg(test)/test-hooks, doc(hidden))}. Creation checks the password (8 NFKC scalars) and KdfParams::validate before any disk access, builds the image via seal::wrap_vk/build_image, and publishes through storage::create_new_atomic_with (hard link, never replaces). Unlock follows CS 9 order (read_bounded, parse, derive MK, open_vault which unwraps VK and verifies the trailer) with no password minimum; wrong password and wrong key both give Authentication. Vault Debug is redacted and keys are ZeroizeOnDrop types. I ran `cargo test -p onlypassword-core vault`: all 14 tests pass, including the every-offset flipped-byte loop. Other points were concluded from reading the code. Only minor issues remain.

Adds Vault::add/get/update/delete/list/search. Each mutation clones the record list, edits it, builds the full image via seal::build_image, checks the record and size limits, re-parses it, writes it atomically, and only then replaces in-memory state. update checks revision overflow before incrementing, keeps created_ms, uses max(now, created_ms), and re-seals with a new item key and nonces. ItemSummary carries no secret fields, and Debug on secrets is redacted. I ran cargo test: 131 passed, 0 failed. I ran as uid 1000, so the read-only-directory test really executes and is not skipped by its root guard. Every acceptance criterion has a test, except the u64::MAX revision case, which the criteria defer to F018; I judged that code correct by reading it only. Minor issues only.

Adds change_master_password, rotate_vault_key and change_master_password_and_rotate_key through one private rekey(). It validates the new password and params first, then derives the current MK and unwraps the VK (Authentication on failure) and cross-checks it against the in-memory VK. It builds and re-parses the full image, writes atomically, and swaps in-memory state only after the write succeeds. Rotation opens each record and re-seals it with fresh IK and nonces, keeping revision and timestamps. The combined op wraps the new VK under the new MK. vault_id and SK are unchanged. This matches crypto-spec 6.5. I ran the 9 rekey tests and they pass; the rest is from reading the code. The only issues are minor.

Adds generator.rs with PasswordOptions (default 20 chars, all classes, require_each on), generate_password (OS source via a new pub(crate) os_source helper) and pub(crate) generate_password_with(&mut dyn RandomSource,..). It follows architecture.md: per-class picks when require_each, fill from the union, Fisher-Yates shuffle, all draws through the existing rejection-sampling uniform_with. The working buffer is Zeroizing and the result is a SecretString. I ran the 13 generator tests and they pass. All acceptance criteria are met; only minor observations remain. No spec deviations, no unsafe, no new dependencies, no spec-issues or dep-requests entries needed.

Adds PassphraseOptions (defaults 7/'-'/false/false), generate_passphrase (OS source) and pub(crate) generate_passphrase_with in generator.rs, re-exported from lib.rs. Validates words 4..=24 and separator <=8 ASCII before drawing, picks words via uniform_with(2048), ASCII-uppercases the first byte, appends one uniform digit to one uniformly chosen word, and holds intermediates in Zeroizing before returning a SecretString. bip39 is listed in approved-deps, added with default-features=false (no features, no rand; Cargo.lock shows only bitcoin_hashes as a dependency), and the feature set is recorded in agent-notes. I ran the generator tests (21 pass). Tests are meaningful: exact word mapping with a fixed-sequence stub, draw counts, boundaries, and Rng failure. No blocker or major issues.

Adds crates/onlypassword-core/src/totp.rs with hotp, totp and totp_for_item. HMAC uses the hmac, sha1 and sha2 crates, all in approved-deps. Dynamic truncation follows RFC 4226, T = unix_secs / period, and no clock is read. Digits must be 6..=8, period 1..=300 and the secret 10..=128 bytes, otherwise InvalidInput. totp_for_item reuses parse_totp_secret from F004. HMAC tags are Zeroizing, and there is no unsafe code and no panicking indexing (slicing uses .get). I ran `cargo test -p onlypassword-core totp` and all 12 tests pass. All KATs load vectors from spec/vectors. There are no spec issues or dep requests to flag.

Adds Vault::export/import (vault/export.rs), MAX_EXPORT_PLAINTEXT, and small refactors in item.rs to share wire types. Header layout, Argon2id on NFKC password, HKDF INFO_EXPORT over pw_key||SK with salt, AD_X = label||header[0..74], the compact fixed-order payload, the CS 9 export-table order (magic, version, flags, kdf ids, KDF bounds, ct_len, decrypt, schema probes, strict pass, conflict, limits), bounded read, single commit write, same-file rejection and the password minimum on export only all match the spec by reading. I ran `cargo test -p onlypassword-core export`: 16 passed. Tests cover every acceptance criterion with real assertions (independent K_x derivation, every-offset flip and truncation loops with the target file unchanged, hand-sealed schema-2 and u64::MAX revision payloads, symlink target). No panics on untrusted lengths (checked arithmetic, .get slicing), and secrets are held in Zeroizing/SecretVec. Minor notes only.

Adds the onlypassword binary: a hand-written exact-spelling parser (--flag=value forms and unknown flags are usage errors, non-UTF-8 argv is a usage error, no secret comes from argv or env), a prompt module (rpassword or bounded --stdin lines, constant-time confirm), static-text error mapping to exit codes 0/1/2/3, a key-file reader (4 KiB cap, from_key_file_text), and init/add-note/get/list/search/delete. init follows the section 5 order (checks, create_new+0600+sync_all, read-back constant-time compare, create_with_key, key-file removal on failure). get masks password, notes, TOTP secret and hidden fields. I ran cargo test -p onlypassword-cli (9 unit + 11 e2e, all pass) and probed the binary by hand: init gives 0600 key and vault, wrong password exits 3 with a one-line message, unknown id exits 1. Deps rpassword/zeroize/tempfile are approved. No blocker or major issues found.

Adds add-login and update with the full architecture.md section 5 item-flag set. The hand-written parser (args.rs item_flags) rejects TOTP parameter flags without --totp, clear+setter conflicts, --notes with --notes-file, bad ranges, and --field without '=' with exit 2, all before any prompt. cmd.rs follows the prompt order master, password, TOTP, notes, hidden values. TOTP goes through normalize_totp_secret, and --url / --field / --totp replace as specified. Note-illegal flags are rejected by core validation with exit 1. I ran cargo test --all-features -p onlypassword-cli and all 9 unit and 16 e2e tests pass. The new e2e tests check stored values through the core library, check revisions for no-change cases, and check argv for secret values. All criteria are met. Only minor findings remain.

Adds passwd [--rotate], rotate-key, export, import, totp and generate (password/passphrase) to the CLI, delegating to the core (change_master_password[_and_rotate_key], rotate_vault_key, export/import, totp_for_item, generators). Prompt order matches architecture.md section 5. Parsing is hand-written with range checks that map to exit 2; export --out is compared to the vault via storage::same_file_path before any prompt. No crypto code is added and no secrets are printed except the deliberate generate/totp output. The only new dependency is serde_json as a dev-dependency, which is on the approved list. I ran `cargo test -p onlypassword-cli`: all tests passed (9 unit, 16 e2e, 12 new e2e_advanced). The remaining checks are from reading the code and tests.

Test-only change: a public-API integration suite (tests/robustness.rs) with a test-local xorshift RNG and a unit test module (vault/robustness_tests.rs) that seals bodies with the internal seal API. No production code changed. I ran both: 14 integration tests and 5 unit tests pass in release/debug with no ignored tests; grep finds no #[ignore] or catch_unwind. Fixtures have control tests, Ok results are compared against original plaintext, failed imports must leave the vault byte-identical, and each unlock/import is timed under 5 s. The only addition outside tests is a self dev-dependency (path, insecure-fast-kdf feature), which is not an external crate.

The new scenario test (definition_of_done_scenario) reads well and covers the brief's steps in order: init, add items, lock/unlock via process exit, read back, passwd --rotate, wrong key exit 3, tampered bytes, export, fresh vault, import with the wrong then the right key file, and a secret-leak scan. However, the commit does not add a new file. It overwrites the existing crates/onlypassword-cli/tests/e2e.rs, which held about 15 CLI integration tests from F019/F020 (1021 lines before, 348 after). Those tests were deleted. CLAUDE.md rule 6 forbids deleting tests, and no other file carries them. Read-only review; I did not run the tests.

Adds a single scenario test (crates/onlypassword-cli/tests/e2e_scenario.rs) driving the real binary with default KDF params through init, add (TOTP/custom/hidden fields, generated password, note), re-read in fresh processes, passwd --rotate (old password exit 3), wrong key exit 3, byte-flipped vault copies (non-zero, empty stdout), export, fresh vault, import (own key file exit 3, first key file succeeds) and list/get --show-secrets equality. It scans every capture for master/new/export passwords and key texts, exempting only --show-secrets and generate. Fake data only. No production code or spec changes, no dep requests. I could not build or run it here (offline, crates unavailable); the gate was reported as passed, and my judgement rests on reading the test. The file is named e2e_scenario.rs rather than e2e.rs because e2e.rs already holds F019/F020 tests, which are untouched; this is documented in the agent note.

Adds the onlypassword-desktop crate (lib+bin, forbid(unsafe_code), panic-free cfg_attr, eframe 0.37 glow/default_fonts/wayland/x11 without persistence, egui, egui_kittest dev-dep, core path dep with test features only in dev-dependencies). view::show draws heading and Locked in a CentralPanel; main.rs is the sole run_native call site. The headless kittest smoke test passes when run by me (cargo test -p onlypassword-desktop --locked). No changes under core, cli, pipeline or spec. The egui 0.37 API deviation (Ui instead of Context) is recorded in spec-issues.md as the closest safe reading. I did not rerun the gate or the cross-target checks; I rely on the notes and the earlier gate pass for those.

Adds ItemIndex (vault/index.rs) and Vault::index(). The index is built in from_parts (create/unlock) with one decryption pass. add/update/delete/import derive the new index from the old one and replace file and index together in commit_with_index, only after persist succeeds. Rekey operations leave the index untouched, which is correct because titles, usernames, URLs, revisions and updated_ms do not change. search applies the lowercase-contains rule to stored summaries. Debug is the fixed string 'ItemIndex { .. }' and Drop zeroizes the owned strings. decrypt_count is gated on test-hooks or cfg(test). There is no file-format or crypto change, and the pilot tests are untouched. I ran `cargo test -p onlypassword-core --features test-hooks` (197 + 14 tests pass, including all 6 new index tests) and `cargo test --workspace` (core and CLI pass). I did not rerun gate.sh. I checked the criteria by reading the tests and code.

Adds pub mod keyfile (read, write_new, ct_eq, private read_from seam) and Vault::create_with_key_file, matching architecture.md 7.1 and the init order of section 5. read uses take(4097) into a Zeroizing buffer, requires UTF-8 and reuses the existing SecretKey::from_key_file_text. write_new uses create_new with mode 0600 on Unix, writes text and newline, calls sync_all and removes the file on failure. create_with_key_file checks the password first, then existence via symlink_metadata and path equality. It then generates the key, writes it, reads it back and compares with a constant-time helper, and calls create_with_key. It removes the key file on any later failure. I ran the 14 keyfile tests as a non-root user (uid 1000), so the unwritable-directory injection really executed. All 14 passed. I did not re-run the full gate or the other crates' tests. No spec, protected-path or dependency changes, and no panics or secret leaks found.

Adds the desktop `error` module (closed UiError enum with literal Display strings, Core variant delegating to the core's Display, From<core::Error>) and the `config` module (Theme, Config defaults 300/30/System/None, validate, ConfigStore::new/platform_default/load/save). Load uses a bounded read (take(4097), rejects >4096), strict UTF-8, a private mirror struct with deny_unknown_fields, a version==1 check and a range check. Every failure returns defaults plus ConfigInvalid and load never writes. Save validates first, writes config.json.tmp with create_new and mode 0600 on Unix, calls sync_all, renames, and removes the tmp file on any failure. Only <dir>/config.json and its tmp file are touched. No unwrap, expect, indexing or arithmetic on file-derived values in non-test code. Dependencies are all in approved-deps.txt. I could NOT build or run the tests: the evaluation container has no crates registry or vendored crates (cargo --offline fails resolving argon2). The verdict rests on reading the code and tests, and on the statement that the gate already passed in a clean container. By reading, every acceptance criterion has a test that can fail. Only minor findings.

Adds SecretBuf, clock (UiClock/SystemUiClock/ManualClock), picker (FilePicker/RfdPicker/ScriptedPicker), the first AppState/Session state machine with open/create/unlock/lock flows, config update of last_vault_path, and the open/create/unlock/browse-placeholder views with a SecretBuf-backed masked TextBuffer adapter. I ran `cargo test -p onlypassword-desktop`: all 31 tests pass (21 unit, 8 session, 1 smoke, 1 kittest). I did not rerun the gate or the Windows/macOS cross-target checks; the generator's note says they passed, and the rfd dependency (default-features off, gtk3) matches spec/approved-deps.txt. By reading: passwords are cleared after every submit and on lock, Debug is redacted for both AppState and SecretBuf, and secrets are moved into SecretString, which zeroizes. No protected paths changed. Only minor test-coverage gaps remain.
